state: The project executes private TypeScript with pinned Bun 1.4.2 and protects immutable Can behavior. A fresh Oxlint 1.85.0 run over authored runtime/ plus tools/runtime/ (vendor ignored) yielded exactly 73 warnings: unused bindings 48, single-argument Array construction 11, control-character regular expressions 6, thenable objects 5, redundant spreads 2, and aliasing this 1. The requested deliverable is a plan for zero warnings, not an immediate code rewrite. Several test inputs deliberately have a then property that can throw; Array(length) sometimes relies on holes or a chosen size; regular expressions reject dangerous bytes; array cloning may be part of resource ownership. No older public ABI needs preservation. Choices include site-specific fixes with documented exceptions, broad linter exclusions, and automatic stylistic replacement. A warning-free run could be enforced with --deny-warnings after behavior checks.

resolution.instructions: Select the safest general treatment of intentional constructs among these lint findings.

criteria.targeted: For each location, distinguish an actual defect from purposeful semantics; remove unused code and clarify safe constructs, using narrowly located explained lint exceptions only where the original behavior must remain.
criteria.global_disable: Turn off noisy rules or skip affected code broadly, leaving only the easy diagnostics to fix.
criteria.mechanical: Apply the suggested syntax substitutions everywhere to satisfy the linter, regardless of sparse-array behavior, adversarial getter tests, or copy semantics.

gate.instructions: Choose when to turn a warning-free lint run into a required check.

criteria.finish_then_gate: Complete repairs and suppressions, run relevant tests and the full runtime suite, then activate --deny-warnings for maintained TypeScript.
criteria.gate_first: Require --deny-warnings before warning cleanup, accepting a temporarily red check during the work.
criteria.no_gate: Do not enforce warning freedom; rely on a one-time cleanup without ongoing prevention.
